title: It's Happening! Unity AI Tech Stack Beta in March
author: Silly_Newt4788

comments.author: NullzeroJP
comments.body:
Smart move.

Tons of AI generation haters when it comes to games. Yes, Slop is a thing. 

But if Unity doesn't get going on the AI train in a serious way... not only will Epic eat their lunch... people will be vibe coding full game engines within 2-3 years... Instead of just Epic/Unity/Godot... we are going to have 50+ free engines out there, that all work on natural language. Unity has to stake their claim. Unity MUST follow suit to keep up with the industry.

That said, they are in a tough position. Their user base (coders, artists, producers) are exact job type that will be largely displaced by AI. They are going to get a BUNCH of push-back. Even with Sentis and their other AI plan... soooo many developers were raging at the thought of Unity produced AI slop. Or stealing artists work, etc.

But I see the writing on the wall. I know what's coming... I've been a coder for decades. The next 1-2 years is probably the last time I will ever write code... This makes me sad to see my life's work... my trade craft... evaporate in the span of 18-24 months... But I'm also excited at the idea of being able to create games without a huge team of artists (not that I don't want to, I just can't pay people's salary). 

Similarly, I'm sure creative artists are also looking forward to creating their exact artistic vision without having to wait a week for a coder to update in-game systems. 

There will be slop. A LOT of slop. But if you are creative, if you have a killer sense of what's fun... I think you will be able execute on your vision like never before. Just... start saving some money, because AI inference costs are going to be stupid high for a little while. ;D

replies.author: NullzeroJP
replies.body:
Heh, yeah I could be off. But when I see agentic work flows… and when I see simple prompts that kick off entire web sites… game engines don’t feel far behind. 

But I can see why many are skeptical. If people only copy paste from a ChatGPT window … or maybe even just watch the occasional AI YouTuber… AI does not look close at all to being ready for game dev. 


Side rant: I think a lot of the “XYZ Model Tested!!” YouTube videos out there do a real disservice to their audiences. They show one shot prompts to “make vampire survivors.” Which tells you almost nothing about how well a model performs. Nobody serious is making software that way.

Anyway… If you look how absolutely insane video generation has come… where the AI generates physics, lighting, sound, VFX… all in high quality and in any style you specify… games are going to end up being the same… maybe not in 2 years… but certainly 5. If it can generate videos with consistent character and environments… there is no reason to think it would stop there… it could easily convert those characters and environments to 3D models and textures. So crazy to think about.

replies.author: sgtpepper171911
replies.body: Yeah it will certainly be interesting (in good and bad ways) to see how far AI can be pushed. UE is open source so in theory an AI has all the data it needs to build an engine. But im skeptical itll be able to manage putting together such a complex piece of software without introducing an ungodly amount of bugs anytime soon. Im a game dev so im obviosuly biased but im skeptical itll be able to make games that can match AA quality any time soon. I do only use AI like youve described though. Bouncing ideas and questions off of chatgpt. I did start making my first website this weekend and im surprised at how many mistakes chatgpt has made through the dev process. Again im going step by step with it as im trying to learn and understand. Im not letting an agent loose in my codebase haha. So i guess i havent truly seen what AI can do at the hands of someone who really knows how to leverage it. Its generative capabilities are obviously super impressive but at the end of the day its just putting colors on a screen. The interactivness and feel of a game is a different ball game. But we shall see. I hope im right but worried im wrong lol.

replies.author: DragonfruitDecent862
replies.body: A month or so ago, i started wondering where software design is, when it comes to "vibe coding". Being a old software and database engineer, i decided to leverage Claude code, and build a bryce 3d raytrace renderer. That turned into making a ENTIRE advanced vulken render-based game engine. Rendering, physics, built in hot reload scripting engine like godot, lightmapping and advanced pbr materials. And it has intergrated, working vr hotseat for testing. When a conpetent user gets their hands on ai like this, and uses it via a CLI, like claude code, or chatgpt codex, thr results are terrifying. Like myself, im sure there are others that have vibe coded heavy applications, but we are already at the point of vibe coding monolithic interdepent code base programs.   Im just in the process of polishing my engine. A terrifying age. And a really odd one.

replies.author: sgtpepper171911
replies.body: As impressive as that sounds. I dont see what is advance about it. It sounds like the bare minimum for a game engine. Is it multithreaded? Have you built a game with it? Can it run AA games at 60 fps? Are the physics interactions high quality. Regardless i think thats the truth of AI, in the right hands competent people can leverage it to build things they probably couldnt before. Im not sure you call it vibe coding if you know what youre doing. Im still not sold AI will just be able to create massive software all by itself or while being directed by someone who has know clue what they are doing, ie vibe coding.

replies.author: DragonfruitDecent862
replies.body: Multi-threaded with Qteditor as the ui framework. Cluster lights. Gpu first approach. Cascaded shadiws with hdr pipeline. This is tech thats been around for ages, its not hard to generate. Can handle around 50,000 objects rotating randomly with realtime light bounce easy. The reason people say ai is slop, and crap, is due to the low effort most idiots put into stuff made with ai. They dont know how to correctly audit a ai after making a vulken or OpenGL renderer from scratch. They dont understand how to troubleshoot and use the ai as a analysis tool.  This is why people say ai is crap, because it normally is for most people using it. Only recently, with CLI tools, have they gotten better.   Your right in that, if i used ai to code the engine, and did it right, i really dont know if we could call it "vibe coding". But the results speak for themselves. Ai, if prompted well by anproper user, can make a engine that outperforms unity. But thats not hard.

comments.author: Gone2MyMetalhead
comments.body:
believe it when I see it. The current AI in Unity 6 is abysmal, and the promise doesn’t match the stack or their in-house expertise. LLMs are massively useful (I use Claude regularly with Unity), but there’s a ton more to even a casual game than the code. 

I’d much rather they actually fixed some larger engine issues than chasing something they’ll almost certainly have no chance of winning at.
